source_event.speaker: user
source_event.text: My unplugged dust-extractor motor got unusually hot and louder than normal—what usually causes that?

source_event.speaker: user
source_event.text: Can you give me a quick, safe way to tell them apart without touching or testing anything energized?

turns.text: Common causes include too much load, blocked cooling airflow, power-supply trouble, or mechanical drag from worn bearings or rubbing parts. Frequent starts, long runs, a hot room, and internal electrical damage can also create excess heat, but those categories alone cannot identify what is wrong with your motor.

turns.text: Keep it off; disconnect every energy source, prevent restart, control stored energy, and allow cooling. Review whether heat followed clogging, longer runs, repeated starts, or electrical work; inspect externally for blocked vents or damage. If permitted, hand-turn the mechanism for drag. Clues aren't conclusive: trips or burning odor need a technician; smoke or flames mean leave and call emergency services.
